fields.name: session_control
fields.description: Human-gated session clearing (session-control) registration: the IdP app the browser ceremony authenticates against. Arms the platform clear tools and the browser clear ceremony when `intent.enabled: true`, or when `clearing.enabled: true` on a gateway that uses markers without intent capture. A gateway using Dtwo authentication needs no credentials here — it gets its organization's platform-provisioned app — but prefer `clearing: {enabled: true}` over an empty block, so the block states what it does: an empty one arms only while `intent.enabled` is true and parks inert otherwise. `client_id` is only needed for a gateway trusting a customer-run IdP, and `redirect_uri` only for one the browser reaches at a different origin than its token audience. The ceremony issuer is not configured here — it is always `gateway.authentication.jwks_info.jwt_issuer` (the same tenant issues both the inbound tokens and the browser-login ID tokens), and the deploy derives `SESSION_CONTROL_ISSUER` from it.

fields.name: log_level
fields.description: ContextForge log level.
fields.rationale: Raise to `DEBUG` or `TRACE` to diagnose a specific issue; lower to `WARNING` or `ERROR` to reduce log volume in production.

fields.name: allowed_origins
fields.description: CORS allowlist; JSON-encoded array in the env file.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: When omitted, defaults to true and authentication is enabled. Sets MCP_REQUIRE_AUTH accordingly.
fields.rationale: Leave at the default `true` for production. Set `false` only for local development where you want an unauthenticated gateway.

fields.name: jwks_info
fields.description: JWT validation settings. Required when the gateway validates bearer tokens directly.

fields.name: sso_issuer
fields.description: SSO issuer URL for generic SSO discovery. Setting this also enables RFC 9728 resource-metadata discovery by default, advertising this issuer to MCP clients; set `mcp_oauth_resource_metadata_enabled: false` to opt out.
fields.rationale: Set when you're using an SSO provider that publishes an OpenID Connect discovery document at `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Only set an issuer you want advertised: MCP clients will follow it for OAuth discovery.

fields.name: jwt_issuer_verification
fields.description: Whether to verify the JWT iss claim.
fields.rationale: Leave unset or `true` — the gateway defaults it to `true` and refuses to start with `false` whenever `jwks_info` is configured, because skipping issuer verification against external IdP keys enables token substitution; the schema rejects `false` for the same reason. Set `true` explicitly to pin the secure value against a future change in the gateway default, not to make a choice.

fields.name: jwt_audience_verification
fields.description: Whether to verify the JWT aud claim.
fields.rationale: Leave unset or `true` — the gateway defaults it to `true` and refuses to start with `false` whenever `jwks_info` is configured, since a token minted for another service in the same tenant would otherwise be accepted here; the schema rejects `false` for the same reason. Set `true` explicitly to pin the secure value against a future change in the gateway default, not to make a choice.

fields.name: require_jti
fields.description: Require a jti claim on each token.
fields.rationale: The gateway defaults this to `true`, so omitting it rejects every request from Auth0 or Entra ID with "Token is missing required JTI claim" — neither IdP mints a `jti` on access tokens. Set `false` for those, and for any other IdP whose tokens lack `jti`; stay at the `true` default only when your IdP emits one and you rely on per-token revocation, since a `jti`-less token cannot be revoked individually.

fields.name: require_token_expiration
fields.description: Require an exp claim on each token.
fields.rationale: The gateway defaults this to `true`, so omitting it already rejects tokens carrying no `exp` claim, which never age out — the setup runbooks set it explicitly only to state that posture. Set `false` only for a short-lived local experiment against an IdP that mints non-expiring tokens, and revert before the gateway sees real traffic.

fields.name: mcp_oauth_resource_metadata_enabled
fields.description: Enable RFC 9728 OAuth resource metadata discovery. When omitted, defaults to true if `sso_issuer` is set; set false to disable explicitly.
fields.rationale: The gateway defaults this to `false`, so discovery is off unless something turns it on. Set `true` when spec-compliant MCP clients must find your authorization server automatically and you have no `sso_issuer` — without it, 401 responses carry no `resource_metadata` URL and the client has nowhere to begin the OAuth flow. With `sso_issuer` set the deploy turns it on for you, so leave it unset there; set `false` to override that and stop advertising the issuer to clients you configure out of band.

fields.name: sso_generic_scope
fields.description: OAuth scope string for the generic SSO discovery flow.
fields.rationale: Set to the OAuth scope your SSO provider requires (e.g. `openid profile email`). Ignored when `sso_issuer` is not set.

fields.name: oauth_dcr
fields.description: OAuth Dynamic Client Registration overrides. Defaults are auto-derived from mcp_servers; set fields here to override (typically to disable DCR/discovery for IdPs that pre-provision clients).

fields.name: well_known_allow_http
fields.description: When true, forces the gateway to grant tokens to http URLs. This is used to run the container in local mode.

crossFieldConstraints.message: When authentication is enabled (the default), "jwks_info" must be configured. "sso_issuer" alone is metadata-only and does not validate tokens.

When authentication is enabled (the default) and "jwks_info" is configured, "jwt_issuer_verification" and "jwt_audience_verification" cannot be false — the gateway refuses to start. Omit them to take the secure default.

sections.title: gateway.authentication.jwks_info
sections.description: JWT validation settings. Required when the gateway validates bearer tokens directly.

fields.name: jwt_algorithm
fields.description: Signing algorithm for bearer tokens.
fields.rationale: Set to the asymmetric algorithm your identity provider signs with — RS256 for most (Auth0, Entra), ES256 for elliptic-curve tenants. The HS256/HS384/HS512 values are symmetric and are rejected here: `jwks_info` always implies a JWKS endpoint, which publishes public keys only, and the gateway refuses to start on that combination.

fields.name: jwt_jwks_uri
fields.description: JWKS discovery endpoint for public keys.
fields.rationale: Set to the JWKS URL your identity provider publishes; the gateway fetches public keys from here to validate incoming tokens. Must begin with a lowercase `https://` — the gateway rejects every other scheme, `file://` included, as an SSRF and key-substitution vector, and refuses to start.

fields.name: jwt_issuer
fields.description: Expected iss claim value.
fields.rationale: Set to the `iss` claim your provider emits; the gateway rejects tokens whose `iss` does not match. Use the `https://` form — the gateway dereferences this URL for `/userinfo` token introspection and refuses to start on `http://`. Auth0 issuers carry a trailing slash and the comparison is exact, so `https://tenant.us.auth0.com/` and `https://tenant.us.auth0.com` are different values.

fields.name: jwt_audience
fields.description: Expected aud claim value.
fields.rationale: Set to the `aud` claim the provider targets at this gateway; prevents tokens meant for other services from being accepted.

crossFieldConstraints.message: When authentication is enabled (the default), "jwt_jwks_uri" must begin with a lowercase "https://" — the gateway rejects every other scheme, "file://" included, as an SSRF and key-substitution vector, and refuses to start.

When authentication is enabled (the default), "jwt_algorithm" cannot be HS256, HS384 or HS512 — a JWKS endpoint publishes public keys, which only verify asymmetric signatures, so the gateway refuses to start. Use RS256 or ES256.

When authentication is enabled (the default), "jwt_issuer" cannot begin with "http://" — the gateway dereferences it for /userinfo token introspection and refuses to start rather than send a bearer token in cleartext.

sections.title: gateway.authentication.oauth_dcr
sections.description: OAuth Dynamic Client Registration overrides. Defaults are auto-derived from mcp_servers; set fields here to override (typically to disable DCR/discovery for IdPs that pre-provision clients).

fields.name: dcr_enabled
fields.description: Enable Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591) against upstream OAuth issuers.
fields.rationale: Set `false` when your IdP (e.g. Entra ID) does not support DCR and OAuth clients are pre-provisioned out of band; leave unset to inherit the default driven by `mcp_servers[*].authentication.issuer`.

fields.name: auto_register_on_missing_credentials
fields.description: Automatically register a client with the issuer when client_id/client_secret are absent.
fields.rationale: Set `false` to require pre-provisioned client credentials and fail closed when they are missing.

fields.name: oauth_discovery_enabled
fields.description: Enable RFC 8414 OAuth authorization-server metadata discovery on the gateway.
fields.rationale: Set `false` when the upstream IdP does not publish authorization-server metadata (common with config-only Entra deployments).

sections.title: gateway.ssrf
sections.description: SSRF protection overrides. Strict defaults apply when omitted.

fields.name: allow_localhost
fields.description: Allow outbound connections to localhost / 127.0.0.1.
fields.rationale: Enable only for local development where the MCP server runs on the same host as the gateway; leaving it on in production widens the gateway's outbound attack surface.

fields.name: allow_private_networks
fields.description: Allow outbound connections to RFC 1918 private networks.
fields.rationale: Enable only when the gateway and MCP server share a private network (e.g. co-located on one EC2 host); prefer `allowed_networks` with a surgical CIDR allowlist in production, since a blanket private-range allow widens the gateway's outbound attack surface.

fields.name: allowed_networks
fields.description: CIDR allowlist for outbound connections; JSON-encoded in the env file.
fields.rationale: Set to the specific CIDRs your MCP servers live on when the gateway must reach private hosts — prefer this surgical allowlist over the blanket `allow_private_networks=true`, since every range you add widens the gateway's outbound attack surface. Shared address space `100.64.0.0/10` (CGNAT — every Tailscale node address, for example) is blocked on every server registration and config import since ContextForge 1.0.7, above every other SSRF setting; a CIDR here that lies wholly inside `100.64.0.0/10` (e.g. `100.64.0.0/10` itself or your tailnet subnet) re-permits those addresses. Broad entries such as `100.0.0.0/8` or `0.0.0.0/0` do not.

fields.name: dns_fail_closed
fields.description: Block the request if DNS resolution fails.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Enable session intent capture. Auto-injects an internal MCP server exposing `set_intent` into the gateway and wires the platform intent-capture policy into the egress pipeline. Users declare intent via `set_intent`; policies read it through the `dtwo.lib.intent_match` library.
fields.rationale: Turn on when you want intent-aware policies to have real values to read. Capture alone never denies a call — but it arms the egress closed-pipeline gate for `set_intent`: customer egress denies, transforms, and marker writes stop applying to that one tool (needed so a customer deny on the set_intent response cannot block the client while the platform capture policy has already committed the intent to session state). Customer INGRESS policies still govern `set_intent` unless `required: true` is also on. No `mcp_servers[]` configuration is needed — the platform intent server is deployed inside the gateway container and injected automatically.

fields.name: required
fields.description: Require an intent to be set before any tool call other than `set_intent`. Injects the platform intent-required policy into the ingress pipeline.
fields.rationale: Turn on when your intent registry and workflows are settled. Requires `enabled: true` — a gate with no capture policy would deny every call forever. Also arms the INGRESS closed-pipeline gate for `set_intent`: customer ingress denies/throttles/argument-inspection stop applying to that one tool (needed so a customer default-deny cannot AND against intent_required and lock the agent out of `set_intent`). Availability note: while on, the gate fails closed, so an intent-server outage blocks the entire tool surface (only `set_intent` stays reachable). A transient OPA/registry blip self-heals — `set_intent` returns a retryable `registry_unavailable` rather than locking permanently — but to recover from a sustained intent-server outage, set `required: false` and redeploy.

crossFieldConstraints.message: `required: true` requires `enabled: true` (a required gate needs the capture policy to write intent).

sections.title: gateway.session_control
sections.description: Human-gated session clearing (session-control) registration: the IdP app the browser ceremony authenticates against. Arms the platform clear tools and the browser clear ceremony when `intent.enabled: true`, or when `clearing.enabled: true` on a gateway that uses markers without intent capture. A gateway using Dtwo authentication needs no credentials here — it gets its organization's platform-provisioned app — but prefer `clearing: {enabled: true}` over an empty block, so the block states what it does: an empty one arms only while `intent.enabled` is true and parks inert otherwise. `client_id` is only needed for a gateway trusting a customer-run IdP, and `redirect_uri` only for one the browser reaches at a different origin than its token audience. The ceremony issuer is not configured here — it is always `gateway.authentication.jwks_info.jwt_issuer` (the same tenant issues both the inbound tokens and the browser-login ID tokens), and the deploy derives `SESSION_CONTROL_ISSUER` from it.

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: Public client id of the dedicated session-control OAuth app (native, PKCE, no client secret). Optional on a gateway authenticating against Dtwo's Auth0: the platform provisions one per organization and renders it at deploy. An explicit value always wins.
fields.rationale: Leave unset on a gateway using Dtwo authentication. Set it only when the gateway trusts your own IdP: the ceremony app must live in the IdP that issues the gateway's inbound tokens, so register a dedicated public client there (authorization-code + PKCE, no refresh grant) and paste its client id here. Do not reuse the gateway API client.

fields.name: redirect_uri
fields.description: Callback URL the browser clear ceremony redirects to, overriding the one the gateway derives from its own token audience. Must be an absolute `https://` URL (`http://` only on localhost, 127.0.0.1, or [::1]). Optional: leave it unset unless the browser reaches the gateway at a different origin than its audience. An explicit value always wins, and the platform allow-lists it verbatim on the IdP application.
fields.rationale: Leave unset in almost all cases — the gateway derives `<origin of the first jwt_audience>/session-control/clear/callback` and the platform registers that. Set it when a reverse proxy or split-horizon DNS puts the browser on a different origin than the audience: give the URL the browser can actually reach, at the root path (`/mcp/*` routes to the streamable-HTTP handler, which rejects browser GETs).

fields.name: clearing
fields.description: Arming control for human-gated clearing.

crossFieldConstraints.message: `clearing.enabled` unset follows `gateway.intent.enabled`; an explicit `true` arms clearing even with intent capture off (the markers-only deployment).
`clearing.enabled: false` while `gateway.intent.enabled: true` is rejected (clearing cannot be withdrawn where markers can block).

While clearing is armed, `gateway.authentication` must be enabled with `jwks_info` — the ceremony binds every clear to the authenticated caller identity, so an unauthenticated inbound leg has nothing to bind.

A gateway that authenticates against an IdP other than Dtwo's Auth0 must set `client_id`: the platform provisions a ceremony app only in its own tenant, and the deploy fails rather than arming a gateway whose ceremony has no application to authenticate against.

`redirect_uri`, when set, replaces the callback the gateway would derive from the first entry of `jwt_audience`, and is the URL the platform allow-lists on the IdP application. Unset, ordering within a comma-separated `jwt_audience` decides the callback.
While clearing is armed, `jwt_issuer` must be a normalized HTTPS URL (it becomes the ceremony issuer via `SESSION_CONTROL_ISSUER`) and `jwt_audience` must not be blank.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Arm human-gated clearing of session intent and markers. Unset follows `gateway.intent.enabled`. `false` while intent is enabled is a deploy error (clearing cannot be withdrawn where markers can block).
fields.rationale: Write `true` whenever you want clearing. It is only strictly *required* on a gateway that runs marker-writing policies WITHOUT intent capture — with intent capture on, the block arms on its own — but stating it makes the block say what it does rather than leaving that to `gateway.intent.enabled`, and it keeps clearing armed if intent capture is later turned off. `false` while intent capture is on is rejected: clearing cannot be withdrawn where markers can block.

fields.rationale: A short memorable identifier shown in the d2 UI.

fields.rationale: One-line summary so end users know what this server offers.

fields.name: url
fields.description: Upstream MCP server endpoint URL.
fields.rationale: Where the gateway forwards MCP requests for this server.

fields.name: transport_type
fields.description: MCP transport protocol. Uppercased and underscore-stripped at emission.
fields.rationale: `http` for most servers; `sse` only when the server explicitly requires server-sent events.

fields.name: authentication
fields.description: Authentication strategy used when the gateway connects to this server.

fields.name: refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: Gateway refresh interval for this server.
fields.rationale: How often the gateway re-fetches the server's tool list. Raise when the list changes rarely, lower when it changes often.

fields.name: visibility
fields.description: Who can discover this server in the UI.
fields.rationale: `public` lists the server to everyone; `team` lists to your tenant only; `private` hides it from discovery.

fields.name: owner_email
fields.description: Contact email for the server owner.
fields.rationale: Who to contact when this server breaks.

sections.title: mcp_servers[].authentication
sections.description:
Authentication strategy used when the gateway connects to this server.
Discriminated union keyed on `type`. Variants:
- `bearer` — see [`mcp_servers[].authentication (bearer)`](#mcp_serversauthentication-bearer)
- `basic` — see [`mcp_servers[].authentication (basic)`](#mcp_serversauthentication-basic)
- `authheaders` — see [`mcp_servers[].authentication (authheaders)`](#mcp_serversauthentication-authheaders)
- `query_param` — see [`mcp_servers[].authentication (query_param)`](#mcp_serversauthentication-query_param)
- `oauth` — see [`mcp_servers[].authentication (oauth)`](#mcp_serversauthentication-oauth)
- `cert` — see [`mcp_servers[].authentication (cert)`](#mcp_serversauthentication-cert)

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for bearer-token auth.

fields.name: token
fields.description: Bearer token sent in the Authorization header.
fields.rationale: Paste the static bearer token the upstream server issued you.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for HTTP basic auth.

fields.name: username
fields.description: Basic-auth username.
fields.rationale: Account name for the upstream server when it uses HTTP basic auth.

fields.name: password
fields.description: Basic-auth password.
fields.rationale: Account password for HTTP basic auth; stored encrypted at rest.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for custom auth-header auth.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: One or more header name/value pairs.
fields.rationale: Use when the server requires a custom header name (e.g. `X-Api-Key`) instead of `Authorization`.

fields.name: key
fields.description: Header name.
fields.rationale: The header name the server expects (e.g. `X-Api-Key`).

fields.name: value
fields.description: Header value.
fields.rationale: The token or key sent in the header.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for query-parameter auth.

fields.name: param_key
fields.description: Query parameter name.
fields.rationale: The URL query parameter name the server reads for auth (e.g. `api_key`).

fields.name: param_value
fields.description: Query parameter value.
fields.rationale: The key or token sent in the query parameter.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for OAuth 2.0 auth.

fields.name: grant_type
fields.description: OAuth grant type.
fields.rationale: Pick the OAuth grant the upstream server supports — `client_credentials` for machine-to-machine, `authorization_code` for delegated user auth.

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: OAuth client ID.
fields.rationale: The OAuth client identifier the upstream server issued you. Omit to let the gateway register dynamically (requires `issuer`).

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: OAuth client secret.
fields.rationale: The OAuth client secret paired with `client_id`. Omit for public clients or when using DCR.

fields.name: token_endpoint_auth_method
fields.description: How the client authenticates to the token endpoint.
fields.rationale: Defaults to `client_secret_post`, which sends `client_id`/`client_secret` in the request body. Set `client_secret_basic` for providers that require an HTTP Basic header and reject a body secret with `invalid_client` — Airtable is one. Ignored on the DCR path: when `issuer` drives dynamic client registration the gateway overwrites this with the method it registered under, so set it only alongside an explicit `client_id`/`client_secret`.

fields.name: token_url
fields.description: OAuth token endpoint.
fields.rationale: The token endpoint the gateway posts to. Omit when `issuer` is set — DCR will discover it.

fields.name: authorization_url
fields.description: OAuth authorization endpoint.
fields.rationale: The authorize endpoint for delegated user flows. Omit for non-interactive grants like `client_credentials`.

fields.name: redirect_uri
fields.description: OAuth redirect URI.
fields.rationale: Callback URL the upstream server redirects back to after user consent.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description: OAuth issuer URL; enables DCR when set without client_id/secret/token_url.
fields.rationale: Set to enable dynamic client registration — the gateway discovers token/authorize URLs and registers itself automatically.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: OAuth scopes requested.
fields.rationale: Scopes the gateway requests from the provider; match the provider's documented scope strings.

fields.name: pkce_enabled
fields.description: Enable PKCE on the authorization flow.
fields.rationale: Enable for public clients where leaking the `client_secret` is a risk.

fields.name: omit_resource
fields.description: Omit the RFC 8707 resource parameter from OAuth authorize/token requests.
fields.rationale: Escape hatch for providers that reject or mishandle the `resource` parameter on authorize, token-exchange, and refresh requests.

fields.name: oauth_quirks
fields.description: Provider-specific compatibility flags.

fields.name: extra_authorize_params
fields.description: Extra query parameters appended to the authorize URL (keys preserve case).

fields.name: token_response_path
fields.description: Dotted path into the token response for nested access tokens.

fields.name: scope_param_name
fields.description: Override the OAuth scope parameter name.

fields.name: scope_separator
fields.description: Separator used when joining scopes.

fields.name: token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: Override for how long access tokens are cached.

crossFieldConstraints.message: OAuth requires either "issuer" or all of "client_id", "client_secret", and "token_url"

fields.name: type
fields.description: Discriminator for client-certificate auth.

fields.name: ca_cert
fields.description: PEM-encoded CA certificate.
fields.rationale: Paste the PEM-encoded CA cert when the upstream server uses a custom CA (mTLS or self-signed).

fields.description: Discriminator for no gateway-managed auth.
